subject: Implementation playbook workshop — scheduling and prep
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: caroline.dunne@blueharbor.ai, tim.lau@blueharbor.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Implementation playbook workshop — scheduling and prep

Hi Caroline + Tim,

Thanks again for the great discovery yesterday — appreciate the clarity on your inference volume targets and the SLOs you care about. We'd like to schedule the 60–90 minute implementation playbook workshop next where we walk through:

- Proposed topology for inference routing, pooling, and fallbacks
- Autoscaling and cost/latency knobs we recommend for your workload mix
- KV/prefix caching approach and a short probe we can run against a staging payload
- Rollout plan and data-flow diagram for private VPC setup (if you go that route)

Proposed time slots (in PDT):
1) Wed Oct 21 — 10:00–11:30
2) Thu Oct 22 — 09:00–10:30
3) Fri Oct 23 — 13:00–14:30

If none of those work, please suggest two times that do. We can also split into a 60-minute high-level architecture + a follow-up 30-minute ops runbook session if you'd prefer.

Prep items we can share ahead of time: a one-page runbook and a sample staging workload to run a short probe. I'm attaching the runbook draft and a link to a shared folder; we can update it after the session.

Agenda and slide/deck will be light and focused on decisions — expected attendee list from our side is: myself (pre-sales), Ben Carter (solutions engineer — infra & KV cache), and Rishi Malhotra (capacity & SLA). Please let me know if you'd like additional folks from our side (security, networking).

Thanks — looking forward to locking this in.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0197

From: Caroline Dunne <caroline.dunne@blueharbor.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Implementation playbook workshop — scheduling and prep

Thanks, Soojin — excited to move forward. Quick note on availability and attendees:

- I'm out Wed afternoon and have a board meeting Thu morning, so Thu 09:00 PDT is tight for me.
- Tim (cc) will be the primary technical lead and can host if I'm pulled into an executive call.
- We'd like to include our SRE lead (Priya Rao) for the parts about autoscaling and VPC. She is in India (IST) so mornings PT are preferable.

Can we do Wed Oct 21 at 08:30–10:00 PT instead? That would hit late afternoon for Priya (21:00 IST) but she's able to attend. If that doesn't work for you, Thu Oct 22 at 16:00 PT would work for our team (Tim + Priya) but I'd prefer the earlier slot so I can join.

Also a couple of Qs before the workshop:
1) How invasive is the staging probe — do we need dedicated test GPUs or can it run against small infra?
2) Do you recommend any pre-uploaded sample traces or tokenized prompts for the caching experiments?

Thanks,
Caroline
CTO, BlueHarbor AI
caroline.dunne@blueharbor.ai
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: caroline.dunne@blueharbor.ai, tim.lau@blueharbor.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 07:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Implementation playbook workshop — scheduling and prep

Caroline — thanks for the context and for flagging Priya. Wed Oct 21 08:30–10:00 PT works for us; I confirmed with Ben and Rishi and we'll be ready.

Quick answers:
- The staging probe is intentionally lightweight: it doesn't require dedicated GPUs. We can run the probe on a small shared instance (1 GPU v100/t4) to exercise the prefix/KV cache and measure tail latency; results are indicative but not identical to your production fleet. If you'd like production-equivalent numbers, we can coordinate a short smoke test on a larger instance during the follow-up ops window.
- We typically ask for a sample set of 200 representative prompts and 20 long-context traces (tokenized) for the caching experiment; I'll upload a template you can drop examples into before the session. If that's too much overhead, Tim can share a small sample and we'll use that.

Agenda will include a 20-minute topology walkthrough, a 25-minute caching/ops demo (including running the probe), 15 minutes for rollout and VPC/QoS discussion, and 10–20 minutes for open questions and next steps.

I've attached the runbook again and added a short checklist for Priya + Tim. Can you confirm attendee list and whether Priya prefers the 08:30 PT slot? Also, what time zone should I add the calendar invite in for Priya (we'll set it to IST for clarity).

Best,
Soojin

Attachment: redwood-implementation-runbook-v1.pdf
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-Runbook-Template
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 22 Oct 2026 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: BlueHarbor playbook workshop — internal coordination

Ben / Rishi — locking in Wed 2026-10-21 08:30–10:00 PT with BlueHarbor (Caroline, Tim, Priya). I've attached the runbook and checklist (shared link above). Quick ops items:

1) Ben — please be ready to demo the KV/prefix cache probe. We'll aim to run it against a small shared GPU node; bring a quick slide on kernel selection/quantization tradeoffs for 10 minutes.
2) Rishi — please prepare a short SLO/throughput plan and a fallback policy example (model variant + region routing) in case they want to discuss capacity commitments.
3) We'll record the session and follow up with the runbook updated to include BlueHarbor-specific recommendations.

No need to involve Security yet unless Priya asks for SOC2 artifacts during the meeting; if that happens, I'll loop in Mina.

Thanks — Soojin

--
